title: POC Kickoff - Data Handling & Benchmarks
customer_attendees: Aisha Malik - Head of Data Privacy
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate Redwood inference for PineBridge's customer-facing insight pipeline. Main priorities: PII handling, redaction in telemetry, retention windows for prompt storage, workload sizing for peak batch vs low-latency queries, and benchmark plan for latency/cost. Agreed next steps: security pack + architecture doc, sample dataset for sanboxing, 2-week benchmark run, and pricing outline for reserved capacity if needed.
topics: Telemetry/logging: what we keep vs scrub
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood Perf Eng), Aisha (PineBridge - Data Privacy), Marco (Platform), Ravi (ML), Sofie (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto gen): POC kickoff focusing on privacy and bench architecture, with emphasis on redaction rules and retention durations.

[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick check — can you hear us ok?
[00:00:05] Aisha: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Jordan.
[00:00:08] Jordan: Sweet. I'm Jordan, AE on the account. With me are Priya, our solutions engineer, and Liam who runs the benchmarking work. We're here to scope the POC — specifically around data handling, retention, and benchmark targets. Can each of you do a 30-second intro?
[00:00:22] Marco: Marco, platform engineering. We're responsible for the infra side — VPCs, networking, and deployment ops.
[00:00:26] Ravi: Ravi, ML lead. I'll own the model selection and evaluation criteria.
[00:00:30] Aisha: Hi, Aisha — data privacy. I'll be defining what's considered PII and what must be redacted before logs leave our environment.
[00:00:36] Sofie: Sofie from procurement, here mostly to track timelines and contracts.
[00:00:00] Jordan: Great, thanks. Priya, do you want to kick with the proposed POC scope?
[00:00:42] Priya: Sure. High level: six-week pilot. Week 0-1: environment setup and security review (SSO, KMS, network). Week 2-3: benchmark run with our synthetic workload and your sample traces, focusing on latency p95 and cost per 1k tokens. Week 4: redaction/telemetry verification. Week 5-6: final pass and success criteria verification for acceptance. Benchmarks include both bursty low-latency queries and steady-state batch throughput.
[00:01:10] Ravi: Quick clarification: by "batch" do you mean async bulk scoring? Or chunked streaming inference?
[00:01:16] Liam: Good question. For us batch is async scoring — high throughput with throughput targets around X tokens per second. We'll also run streaming latency tests that emulate chat-style calls.
[00:01:28] Marco: On the security side I wanted to call out that we likely need a VPC deployment or Private control plane because of our data residency rules. Is that supported for a short pilot?
[00:01:36] Priya: We can do a Private deployment into a customer-managed VPC for the pilot. Usually for a short POC we spin up a temporary private control plane with strict networking rules — customers can bring their own KMS or use Redwood's managed keys if allowed. Aisha, which KMS mode would you prefer?
[00:01:50] Aisha: We need to review KMS integration. Ideally customer-managed keys — we don't want any plaintext storing on Redwood side.
[00:01:57] Priya: Totally understood. We support external KMS/HSM integrations. We'll include a KMS design in the security pack.
[00:02:05] Jordan: Let's talk data flow. Ravi, can you describe what PII typically looks like in your prompts and telemetry?
[00:02:12] Ravi: Most of our prompts are customer-support transcripts that include names, account numbers, last4s, occasional addresses. We strip obvious tokens client-side but we're looking to quantify residual sensitive tokens that slip through and test our redaction rules. Also want to see how Redwood logs inputs — e.g., do you persist full prompts in telemetry by default?
[00:02:32] Priya: By default our hosted logs keep a trace id and model metadata. For Private deployments we can configure prompt retention to zero or to an encrypted store with the retention window you set. We also have an optional prompt-scrubbing pipeline that runs regex and NER-based redaction before logs hit disk.
[00:02:50] Aisha: Can you be more specific about what "optional" means? We need guarantee we won't have free-text prompts logged in plaintext anywhere.
[00:02:58] Priya: Understood. For the POC we can enable the scrubbing pipeline and set telemetry retention to 0 days for raw prompts. We will still retain minimal telemetry such as request ids, model version, token counts, latency metrics. Anything that could identify a user we can either hash or redact. We'll document where keys and hashes are stored.
[00:03:18] Marco: And what about KV cache? Our use case involves retrieval augmented generation with session state. Is the KV cache persisted to disk? That's a sensitive surface.
[00:03:26] Liam: KV cache in our runtime is in-memory by default for performance. We do have optional checkpointing for longer sessions — but for the POC we recommend in-memory only to avoid persisting session tokens. That will also give you the best latency numbers.
[00:03:40] Aisha: Ok, in-memory only is preferable. However we need to test a failure scenario where a node is restarted — does the system repopulate without writing prompts to persistent logs?
[00:03:49] Priya: Good test. We can simulate node restart during the benchmark and confirm the behavior; we'll capture only aggregate metrics, not raw prompts.
[00:03:58] Ravi: On retention windows: we'll need a configuration where prompt retention is 0, but we want to keep derivation metadata for 90 days for debugging. Is that workable?
[00:04:07] Priya: Yes. We separate "prompt_payload" retention from "telemetry meta" retention. Prompt_payload can be set to never persist. Telemetry meta can be retained up to 90 days — and can be encrypted and access-controlled.
[00:04:20] Aisha: Who has access to that telemetry meta? Is there audit logging for readers?
[00:04:24] Priya: Yes, RBAC integrates with your SSO; we can configure roles so only your security and RM teams have read access. All reads are auditable and we can ship audit logs to your SIEM.
[00:04:35] Marco: Good. On workload sizing, we gave you the QPS distribution in the pre-call doc but to summarize: peak concurrent requests of ~800 qps during batch windows, avg 120 qps, median latencies target p95 < 250ms for streaming small prompts — can you size GPU/eval for that?
[00:04:51] Liam: We'll take that offline for precise sizing but initial thought is a mix of T4-equivalent nodes for batch and A100-class for latency-sensitive lanes. For Private we can provision mixed pools and route by policy (cost vs latency). We'll detail a recommended cluster topology in the Perf plan.
[00:05:09] Jordan: Success criteria — what would make this POC a success from your perspective, Ravi?
[00:05:13] Ravi: Three things: (1) p95 latency on chat flow under 300ms for our 90th percentile prompt size, (2) redaction catches > 99% of defined PII tokens in test corpus, (3) cost per 10k tokens under our target threshold — we have internal number but we can share after call.
[00:05:29] Aisha: Add (4) zero retention of raw prompts and provable access logs for telemetry reads.
[00:05:35] Jordan: Perfect. We'll capture those as acceptance criteria.
[00:05:38] Sofie: From procurement — how long will the trial resources be billed and what's the estimate if we need reserved capacity?
[00:05:45] Jordan: For a pilot we typically offer a timeboxed usage agreement — you pay for the infra you provision. If you decide to move to reserved capacity we can provide a committed quote for monthly usage; Liam can follow up with ballpark numbers.
[00:05:58] Liam: I'll prepare a cost sensitivity matrix: reserved commit vs on-demand vs mixed.
[00:06:03] Marco: On encryption at rest — will Redwood hold any plaintext on your side?
[00:06:07] Priya: No, if you choose customer-managed KMS, we never have the plaintext keys. Anything at rest will be encrypted with your key. We'll include a diagram showing key flow in the security pack.
[00:06:20] Aisha: What about redaction accuracy — you said NER-based scrubbing. Do you have a way to fold our custom regex and a blocklist?
[00:06:28] Priya: Yes, the scrubbing pipeline supports pluggable rulesets: built-in NER models + customer regex/blacklist. For the POC we can ingest your blocklist and run an evaluation over your sample traces and report false positive/negative rates.
[00:06:44] Ravi: We'll provide a sanitized sample of 20k prompts and a second set of 5k with known PII tokens to test recall.
[00:06:51] Jordan: Great. Timeline confirm — six weeks total, with benchmarks in weeks 2-3. Any blockers to that schedule?
[00:06:58] Marco: We need internal approvals to open the VPC peering and to allocate a service account for KMS access — that could take 5-7 business days.
[00:07:06] Priya: We can front-load the security review so networking approvals can happen in parallel with the baseline infra.
[00:07:12] Aisha: Also need legal review for data processing addendum — we have a template. Sofie will coordinate.
[00:07:18] Sofie: Yes, I'll send the DPA template after this call.
[00:07:22] Jordan: Perfect. Bench specifics — Liam, what's the benchmark plan shape?
[00:07:25] Liam: We'll run two suites: a latency suite (chat-style, many short prompts, measure p50/p90/p95) and a throughput suite (bulk scoring with synthetic tokens to stress throughput). For latency we recommend a replicated client across 10 ephemeral clients to emulate concurrent users. For throughput we'll run sustained 1-hour and 4-hour runs. We'll also run a failure/chaos test to simulate node restarts and confirm no prompt persistence.
[00:07:50] Ravi: Will you run the benchmark against our model or your curated open models? We plan to test a fine-tuned model — can that be loaded?
[00:07:58] Priya: We support customer model artifacts in Private deployments; you'll provide the container or model weights and we can stage it in the private environment. For hosted we have restrictions. For the POC if you want private loader, we'll coordinate artifact transfer via a secure bucket.
[00:08:12] Marco: Artifact transfer will need the signed S3 policy.
[00:08:15] Priya: We'll send an artifact transfer guide.
[00:08:19] Aisha: A couple of edge questions — do you tokenize differently in different quantization profiles? Could that affect PII detection?
[00:08:27] Liam: Tokenization doesn't change by quantization. However, certain quantized kernels might alter output fidelity in edge cases; for PII detection we run scrubbing pre-tokenize so it's not impacted. We'll outline the pipeline order: pre-scrub -> tokenize -> inference -> post-filter.
[00:08:44] Jordan: Any competitors or alternatives you're evaluating that we should be aware of?
[00:08:47] Marco: We're also looking at a few others — Anthropic's infra offering and an internal infra team doing on-prem hosting.
[00:08:52] Aisha: Also smaller managed vendors for redaction-centric products.
[00:08:55] Jordan: Good to know. We'll highlight where Redwood differentiates — unified runtime, configurable retention, and inlined scrubbing.
[00:09:03] Sofie: For contract stuff — if we go into reserved capacity what's the minimum term?
[00:09:07] Jordan: Standard reserved terms are 3 or 12 months; we can do a 3-month bridge pilot if you'd like.
[00:09:12] Sofie: Noted.
[00:09:14] Priya: On observability: we'll provide trace-level dashboards showing token counts, per-request latency, per-model cost, and a telemetry feed where we can redacted-sample the prompts if you opt in. This feed can be routed to your SIEM.
[00:09:28] Marco: Can we get sample dashboards ahead of time?
[00:09:30] Priya: Yes — I'll drop a dashboard link and the sample JSON.
[00:09:34] Jordan: Ok wrapping — let's restate concrete next steps and owners.
[00:09:40] Priya: Action items I'll record: 1) Security pack including KMS diagram and audit flow (Priya). 2) Perf plan and cost matrix (Liam). 3) Artifact transfer guide and S3 policy (Jordan). 4) PineBridge to share sanitized sample prompts and PII blocklist (Ravi/Aisha). 5) Procurement/Legal to share DPA template (Sofie).
[00:09:58] Aisha: We'll aim to deliver samples within 3 business days.
[00:10:01] Sofie: Legal will try to turn around the DPA in a week.
[00:10:04] Marco: I'll start the VPC approval request today — expect 5-7 business days.
[00:10:09] Jordan: Great. Anything else?
[00:10:12] Ravi: One last ask — can you run a small test to show redaction false positives? We want to see cases where names get redacted incorrectly.
[00:10:19] Priya: Yes, we'll include a quick false-positive report during the scrubbing eval.
[00:10:24] Jordan: Alright, thanks everyone. We'll send a recap and the security pack by EOD tomorrow.
[00:10:31] Sofie: Thanks all.
[00:10:33] Meeting End
